newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Shots wound three Moslems in Sarajevo--NATO.
newsitem.headline: Shots wound three Moslems in Sarajevo--NATO.

text.p: Three Bosnian Moslems were wounded by gunshots in two separate incidents in the ethnically disputed Sarajevo suburb of Dobrinja early on Sunday, NATO said.

Two of the victims, civilians, were beaten and shot in the legs, said NATO spokesman Major Brett Boudreau. They were taken to hospital, "gravely injured". A third victim, a policeman, was wounded later and also taken to hospital, Boudreau reported.
"Dobrinja is certainly heating up. We have sent additional forces into the area but now that it's daylight the situation seems calm," the NATO spokesman said.

Dobrinja is a community of mid-rise flats built as housing for the 1984 winter Olympic games. It lies west of Sarajevo's city centre, near the airport and an administrative boundary line between Bosnia's Moslem- Croat federation and its Serb republic bisects the settlement.
The exact location of the line is disputed between the parties and has been the occasion for a number of violent incidents in recent months.
